intro: You can use Notion for event coordinators on Mac by building centralized databases for vendors, guest lists, and event schedules. By combining Notion with Lazur, you can quickly dictate notes, find specific database views, and manage your daily task list without leaving your workspace.

blocks.text: Setting up your event dashboard in Notion

To start, create a master page for each event. Use the Notion desktop app on your Mac for the best performance. Press ⌘ N to open a new page. Type /database to select a table view for your master vendor list. This keeps contact info, contract status, and payment deadlines in one column-rich view.

Many coordinators struggle with fragmented information. Use a single source of truth. Create a database for tasks and another for vendors. Link them using the Relation property. This lets you see which vendor is tied to which task without clicking away. If you get stuck on the interface, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the Relation property is located.
Using Notion templates to save hours

Manual data entry is the biggest time sink for event planners. Every event has similar phases: venue booking, catering, marketing, and onsite logistics. Create a database template for each project type. When you start a new event, click the arrow next to the blue New button in your database. Select your template to populate the page with pre-built checklists and property fields.

items: Create a venue scouting checklist as a template.
Add a status property to track progress from Pending to Confirmed.
Include a date property for booking deadlines.
Use a formula property to calculate remaining days until the event.

blocks.text: Managing your Mac workflow with Lazur

Lazur helps you stay in flow while you work in Notion. When you are deep in a spreadsheet and need to check a reminder, you do not need to hunt for the app. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to show your Apple Reminders list. It will point to the information on your screen or answer out loud.

If you are dictating meeting notes after a vendor call, use the fn key. Hold it down to start dictation. Speak your notes clearly. Lazur types them directly into your Notion page at the cursor position. This is much faster than typing when you are tired after a long day of coordination.
Common mistakes in Notion for event management

items: Keeping all info on one massive page instead of using databases.
Forgetting to set permissions when sharing pages with external vendors.
Overcomplicating the workspace with too many nested sub-pages.
Not using the desktop app's ⌘ P search feature to find items fast.
Manually re-typing event details instead of using database properties.

blocks.text: Advanced tips for your event database

Use the Kanban board view for your task management. Press /board to insert one. Drag tasks between columns like Not Started, In Progress, and Done. This visual layout helps you see bottlenecks in your event schedule. If you need to filter this view to show only today's tasks, ask Lazur to guide you to the filter menu.

Ensure your Mac is running macOS 13 or later to keep the Notion app stable. If the app feels slow, press ⌘ R to reload. Check the Notion menu in the top bar to ensure you are on the latest version. This keeps your shortcuts and features working as expected.

faq.question: Can I use Notion offline for event planning?
faq.answer: Notion requires an internet connection to sync your data. You can view cached pages offline, but you cannot edit databases or add new items reliably.

faq.question: How do I share my event schedule with vendors?
faq.answer: Click the Share button at the top right of your page. Invite vendors via email or copy the public link. You can set permissions to 'Can view' so they see the schedule without editing your master list.

faq.question: Is Notion safe for sensitive event data?
faq.answer: Notion uses standard encryption. For highly sensitive data like credit card numbers or private contracts, consider using a secure document vault instead of a standard Notion page.

faq.question: How does Lazur help with Notion on my Mac?
faq.answer: Lazur lets you ask questions about your screen, dictate notes directly into Notion, and get guided help for finding specific settings or menus without clicking through the UI.
